claims.statement: After reverting allocation rule set to v17, the 186 originally-stuck orders remain in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' and new east-node allocations are also being held
claims.limitation: Indicates the root cause is not specific to v18 rule logic, but rather a condition affecting the east-node routing or east-node subsystem itself

claims.statement: root_001 (v18 creates split-reservation orders with excessive carrier latency) contradicted by obs_008 (reverting v18 does not resolve held orders)
claims.limitation: Revert was the test of the hypothesis; failure of mitigation indicates the hypothesis was incomplete or incorrect

claims.statement: The east-node subsystem (dock, carrier integration, or pickup slot management) has a capacity or integration failure affecting all orders routed to it after approximately 05:58, independent of allocation rule version
claims.limitation: East-node orders booked before 05:58 under v17 were confirmed normally; orders from ~06:00 onward (under both v18 and post-revert v17) are held, suggesting an east-node boundary condition rather than allocation-rule-specific defect

claims.statement: East node dock capacity was exceeded or carrier pickup scheduling failed at approximately 05:58, preventing any new orders from being handed off to carriers regardless of allocation rules
claims.limitation: East node may have hit capacity, or carrier system integration (not carrier operations on-call) may have failed; requires dock diagnostics to discriminate

dispositions.rationale: Mitigation (revert_allocation_ruleset) did not resolve the condition; held orders persist and new east-node orders are also held, indicating the root cause is not v18's split-reservation logic but rather a condition in the east-node subsystem or its environment
v18 remains a necessary condition for EXC-0921 scope, but is not the sufficient condition for orders being held; east-node routing is the discriminating factor
Hypothesis that v18 causes split-reservation incompleteness contradicted by revert outcome; split reservations per se may not be the mechanism

contradictions.description: root_001 claims v18 creates the stuck-order condition; obs_008 shows reverting v18 does not resolve stuck orders, indicating root_001 is incorrect or incomplete

next_action.rationale: The revert to v17 preserved the stuck-order condition and introduced new held orders on east node. This strongly suggests a capacity or integration issue at the east-node dock itself. Checking dock capacity will determine if the east node is over-booked, at capacity limits, or has a carrier pickup scheduling failure that prevents order handoff regardless of allocation rules. This is the highest-information diagnostic to isolate whether the problem is supply-side (capacity) or demand-side (carrier integration failure).
